definitions.explanation: A principle or system in which people are evaluated, promoted, or rewarded based on their actual achievements and results rather than seniority, background, or other factors.

examples.japanese: この{会社|かいしゃ}は{実績|じっせき}{主義|しゅぎ}だ。
examples.english: This company operates on a merit-based system.

examples.japanese: {実績|じっせき}{主義|しゅぎ}の{導入|どうにゅう}で{給与|きゅうよ}{体系|たいけい}が{変|か}わった。
examples.english: The introduction of a performance-based system changed the salary structure.

examples.japanese: {年功序列|ねんこうじょれつ}から{実績|じっせき}{主義|しゅぎ}に{切|き}り{替|か}える{企業|きぎょう}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: More companies are switching from seniority-based systems to meritocracy.

examples.japanese: {実績|じっせき}{主義|しゅぎ}には{長所|ちょうしょ}もあるが、{短期的|たんきてき}な{成果|せいか}ばかりを{追|お}うリスクもある。
examples.english: Meritocracy has its advantages, but there is also a risk of only chasing short-term results.

notes:
A compound of {実績|じっせき} (actual results; track record) and {主義|しゅぎ} (-ism; principle). Refers to evaluating people based on what they have actually accomplished rather than on tenure, age, or connections.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {実績|じっせき}{主義|しゅぎ}を{導入|どうにゅう}する: to introduce a merit-based system
- {実績|じっせき}{主義|しゅぎ}の{人事|じんじ}: merit-based personnel management
- {実績|じっせき}{主義|しゅぎ}に{基|もと}づく: based on meritocracy
- {徹底|てってい}した{実績|じっせき}{主義|しゅぎ}: thoroughgoing meritocracy

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {成果|せいか}{主義|しゅぎ}: outcome-oriented approach — nearly synonymous but emphasizes end results more than track record
- {能力|のうりょく}{主義|しゅぎ}: ability-based system — focuses on inherent capability rather than demonstrated performance
- {年功序列|ねんこうじょれつ}: seniority system — the traditional Japanese system that {実績|じっせき}{主義|しゅぎ} often replaces
